book noun

also get out your book, take up your book, classroom commands, in circulation (of books), cloth-bound book, hardback, hardcover book

classical

Traupman 28
Traupman 164

liber, librī m.

noun, second declension · Declension on Wiktionary

With a short first vowel; distinguish līber, “free.”

Examples

  • Quem librum legāmus?

    Which book shall we read?composed

  • Librum in manum, librōs in manūs capite.

    Get out your book (your books).Traupman 33

  • Librum prōme (librōs prōmite).

    Get out your book (your books).Traupman 33

  • librōs inde prōmere

    to take books out of thereCic. Fin. 3.7 (Lewis & Short s.v. prōmō)

  • In manūs sūme (sūmite).

    Take it up (to read or study).Traupman 34

  • in manibus esse

    to be in circulation (of books)Traupman 291

  • liber līnō contēctus

    a cloth-bound bookTraupman 292

See also page, read, story.

SourcesLewis & Short: liber

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
